objective_for_doctor: A 4-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have significant dyspnea, nasal congestion or a clear runny nose, and noticed that you produce more saliva than usual.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m having a lot of trouble breathing, like it’s hard for me to catch my breath. I also have a stuffy or runny nose, and I’ve been drooling more than usual. I’ve noticed a kind of noisy breathing (stridor), and it seems worse at night.

Doctor: I’m going to ask a few quick questions to figure out what’s going on—does the noisy breathing sound like a high-pitched stridor mainly when you breathe in, and has he had any fever? Also, is his voice muffled or is he refusing to swallow, and when was this started?  
Doctor: If you can, tell me whether the symptoms are worse when he lies flat and whether he’s had any choking episode or new exposure (smoke, sick contacts), and does he drool because swallowing hurts.

Yes, it sounds like a high-pitched noise when he breathes in. I’m not sure about fever. His voice isn’t muffled that I’ve noticed, and he isn’t refusing to swallow—he’s just drooling more than usual. This started recently, and it seems worse at night. I don’t know about choking or any new exposures like smoke or sick contacts.

Doctor: I’m going to listen to his breathing and check his throat for swelling; also, has he had any barking cough or wheeze, and is he able to speak/cry normally?  
Doctor: Any history of allergies/eczema or similar episodes, and can you estimate whether drooling started at the same time as the stridor (or later)?

He does have a barking cough, and I’ve noticed the noisy breathing more than wheezing. He can cry and make normal sounds, not like he can’t speak. We don’t know about allergies or eczema, and the drooling started around the same time as the noisy breathing.

Doctor: I’m going to examine his throat and neck for swelling/foreign body and listen closely for inspiratory stridor; quick follow-up—does he seem to pull in around the ribs/neck when breathing, and is his breathing worse when calm or crying vs only at night?  
Doctor: Also, has he had any recent viral symptoms, and do you notice a fever or hot body at home?

I think he does pull in a bit around his ribs/neck when he breathes. His breathing seems worse at night, and it’s pretty bad even when he’s calm. We’ve had some viral-type symptoms like a runny/stuffy nose, but I don’t know about fever or if he’s been hot at home.

Doctor: Given the inspiratory stridor, barky cough, nighttime/worse-when-flat breathing effort, and new drooling starting with symptoms, I’m most concerned about **upper airway obstruction**—I want to urgently check his oxygen level and airway status; please answer: has he had any stridor at rest with trouble swallowing/working harder to breathe, and is he drooling to the point of needing to spit constantly?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry (SpO2) and, if available urgently, **neck/airway lateral X-ray** to look for croup/epiglottitis; also tell me whether his vaccination status (especially Hib) is up to date.

Yes—he has the noisy breathing even when he’s resting, and he seems to be working harder to breathe. He is drooling a lot, like he needs to spit pretty often, but he hasn’t been refusing to swallow.  

I’m not sure about his Hib vaccination status.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as a potentially life-threatening upper-airway cause—before imaging, I want urgent vitals and an exam for airway emergency; does he have any fever, and can he handle his secretions (is drool increasing or pooling)?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Immediate Pulse_Oximetry (SpO2) + Respiratory rate/work of breathing assessment; REQUEST TEST: Lateral Neck_X-Ray (or direct visualization by ENT if available urgently) and check if he is drooling beyond what he can clear.

I don’t know if he has a fever. His drooling feels like it’s increasing and it sometimes seems like it’s pooling because he has to spit pretty often. His breathing looks fast and like he’s working harder to breathe.

Doctor: This combination—**inspiratory stridor at rest, worsening work of breathing, and progressively increasing drooling/secretions pooling**—is concerning for a **significant upper-airway obstruction**, so we need to act urgently; I’m going to get his oxygenation and arrange an immediate airway assessment.  
Doctor: **REQUEST TEST: Immediate Pulse_Oximetry (SpO2)** and **REQUEST TEST: Lateral Neck_X-Ray** (or ENT/ED direct visualization if X-ray will delay care).

Okay. Please check his oxygen level right away and get someone to look at his airway urgently. He’s still having the noisy breathing at rest, and the drooling is definitely more than usual—it keeps building up and he has to spit often.

Doctor: I’m treating this as an emergency for upper-airway obstruction—please confirm his SpO₂ now and bring him to the ED/ENT for immediate airway assessment, because worsening stridor at rest with increasing drooling suggests a tight lesion.  
Doctor: I’m going to assume the likely diagnosis is **epiglottitis** unless imaging/ENT shows otherwise—does he have a high fever or appear very toxic, and is neck extension painful/limited?  

REQUEST TEST: Immediate Pulse_Oximetry (SpO2) and full set of vitals (temp, HR, RR)  
REQUEST TEST: Lateral Neck_X-Ray (if it won’t delay ENT visualization) or immediate ENT/direct visualization  
Doctor: **DIAGNOSIS READY: Epiglottitis (upper-airway obstruction due to epiglottic inflammation), pending urgent ENT confirmation**

[DDX]
1. Epiglottitis
